title: Casper Holstein, Dutch Schultz and Owney Madden
summary: Greer names who controlled the numbers and says Owney Madden was top.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Did you ever meet -- there was a rich guy up in Harlem during those years who was kidnapped at one time, Casper Holstein (PHONETIC).

Casper Hostein, I know him, the number man. Yeah, he was one of the few colored guys -- he was a numbers back-up. They kidnapped him, sure. But they turned him loose because he was closely associated. 'Cause they put the word out, "turn him loose." Whenever the Syndicate says, "that's my man," that was it. That was it.
Now, when you first came to New York, who controlled the numbers?

I've seen him. But my man was the top man. My man was a top man. He was over Dutch Schultz, Al Capone and all of them. He wasn't a -- a little, tiny guy. Talked like a girl. Never raised his voice. Owney Madden. Owney Madden. He owned the Cotton Club. When he said something, that was it. And he loved -- he loved Duke because him and Duke used to sit up and play "Grits" and all that, "Coon Can" all night long after the club closed. Me, I'm ready to run. When the last note hit, I'm gone. I say, I don't play that game, I don't know anything about them games.
